taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 16.8 | 2.56 | 2.56
2 | 73.3 | 10.4 | 12.9
3 | 701 | 49.9 | 62.9
4 | 51.6 | 51.4 | 114
5 | 99.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as Q-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Court-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis. The VES interpretation reveals a five-layer sequence. Resistivity begins at 16.8 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (Layer 1), increases through 73.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (Layer 2) to a peak of 701 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (Layer 3), then decreases to 51.6 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (Layer 4) before rising again to 99.8 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (Layer 5). Based on this sequence, the curve type is AKH. Please note that the Q-type classification currently on file is incorrect and does not align with the interpreted resistivity values.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKH", "label_issue_flagged": true}
